Intro Call: Oct 28th, 2024

Participants

  • Grupo Alifin: Fernando Padilla (CEO Grupo Alifin) / Alejandro Creixell (CEO at Cretum Partners - financial advisor)
  • SixPoint: Jose / Alejandro


Grupo Alifin Overview

With a 17-year track record in private credit, Grupo Alifin operates through key subsidiaries:

  1. Pretmex – Specializes in credit, leasing, and factoring services. Portfolio size: USD 40 million.
  2. Lendera – A crowdfunding marketplace facilitating alternative financing with lower interest rates.
  3. Valto – A private debt fund for financial SMEs, with a portfolio size of USD 3 million.

Financing Terms and Funding Sources

Grupo Alifin provides financing terms of 36 to 60 months, primarily funded through bank loans, securitizations in the capital markets, and equity. They are currently seeking to diversify their funding sources, targeting a cost of capital at or below 20-25%.

- Sary started with working on how they can make the wholesale market online and they started with being a marketplace/ecommerce for suppliers and merchants
- Sary is a B2B platform that connects small businesses with wholesalers and brands in one place to enable an effective and efficient way of doing business. - Their goal is to be in the end-to-end channel. Thus they have started with POS and logistics services. Currently, they have 4000 businesses connected to POS services and do around$ 50-60MN of transactions. They are planning to launch the payment channel into it

- They do $75MN transactions monthly, 25MN in marketpplace and 50MN in POS
- The platform is currently 100% equity funded and is seeking debt finance to grow the merchant finance business. Currently the loan book is $10m and Sary plans to grow it to between $30m - $40m. The platform offers access to traceable pharmaceutical and medical products from multiple vendors in addition to providing fulfillment, demand planning, and inventory financing.

The platform provides both a marketplace to connect supplier and pharmacies and also hold their own inventory which they sell.

The company works with all stakeholders across the value chain including the following: manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, and pharmacies. 

Operations in Egypt began in January 2022 and credit financing to pharamacists is done by third party financiers. Sales in Egypt average $2m per month. Embedded 2% interest rate. The aim is for the $2m average sales to increase to $5m by December 2024 with 50% of those 

Operations in Tanzania began in September 2023 and Grinta provides credit terms directly to pharmacists. In Tanzania, they are the sole distributors of 2 pharmaceutical companies that are manufactured in Egypt. The plan is to grow this number and become sole distributors for more manufacturers. Tanzania imports ~90% of its pharmacieutical supplies.


- Updated in November 2024:
- In Egypt their sales is purely based on cash, but a small part of their sales is with a third party financier. The sales team, underwriting and collection, everything is with this third party and Grinta do not have any in house capabilities for this

- The financing option for this third party is integrated in their order processing where the pharamcies have the option to choose this pay through financier option. However, all the responsibilities in term of providing knowledge about the financing and everything lies with the third party

- They have been focusing their equity to expand into new markets, develop tech and do capex. 

- And another reason they did not allocate anything to financing themselves was that they lack the credit risk and credit experience in total and they are looking for an experienced partner who can help them structure and introduce this credit product in the market and also pool funds with them 

- They can double down their current sales figures in Egypt if they introduce the credit sales

- They don't have complete access to the data for all the credit sales done through their platform for the third party financier


- We proposed that we need to see around 5% monthly cost of financing in Egypt if we want to partner for a potential facility. Grinta team was skeptical about this rate as it is double of the current bank rate

- Grinta team agreed to scout the market for biggest players in the Egyptian markets providing factoring and similar type of financing to provide how much they charge in the market

- They are open to us guiding them how they can start the pilot in Egypt and what they need to do, like term, interest rates, no of months sample etc. They can start with the 5% monthly rate and see how it fly in the market and with the pharmacies. They can do this at their cost and equity, but will require our guidance in how to structure it, the risk assessment, credit scoring, etc.

[{"update":"

Latests KPIs (as of Dec 31st, 2024)

Onboarding

Total released users: 2,043

Waitlist signups: 36,094

Onboarding funnel rate (invited-to-released): 19%

Credit model approval rate: 49%


Usage

Active users rate (avg 2024): 85%

Total purchased value: $436,388

Loan portfolio: $72,311


Other

MRR December: $5,005 (71% growth vs Sept’24)

Ancillary revenue December: $963 (116% growth vs Sept’24)

Default risk at DPD 90: 1.9%

Churn: 2.3%


Wins

  • December was a record-breaking month. We reached 2,000+ users and processed over $100K USD in transactions, a 51.7% increase compared to November. In total, we handled 9,400 purchases, received 3,300 payments, and almost 90% of our customer base was active. Similar to Q3, our infrastructure and team of five (5) was able to handle this growth seamlessly. 
  • Our gamified loyalty program, Guama Pro, is showing promising results on default risk metrics as users progress to higher levels. We’ve observed a 3x improvement for Bronze users and a 6x improvement for Silver users across all repayment maturities. Although more data is still needed, if this trend continues, we’ll be able to offer exciting benefits (e.g., no monthly fee) to customers as they graduate without affecting unit economics. 
  • Since November we are charging interest to our entire user base. This was the last phase to complete our core credit platform due to the complexity it posed on monthly billing. To date, we have not received any customer complaints, and our billing system is working without issues. 
  • In December, our net CAC was $0.02 USD, driven by an increase in ancillary revenue from the launch of Apple & Google Pay. As context, when users get onboarded they are given the option to purchase the physical card ($5) or activate Apple/Google pay ($2). In December, 80% of new customers acquired at least one of the two products. 
  • Once again, our product and tech team delivered an impressive set of new features (see below), further consolidating our position as one of the most advanced credit cards in the Colombian market. 


Q4 product releases


Cash advances: withdrawals transferred in real-time to the user’s bank account, charged against their card’s line of credit. 

Account customization: 

Notification preferences: users can now select through which channel they receive notifications (push, email, or both) for purchases and payments.

Installment preferences: users can now preset the number of installments for each purchase, based on the type of purchase (e.g., international or virtual).

Apple & Google Pay: wallet activation through the app (push provisioning) and checkout screens to pay the activation fee ($2). Since its release, nearly 30% of all transactions are made using this payment method.

Interests: for transactions deferred to two or more installments, interest is charged and billed on a monthly basis.


Challenges

  • Our payment provider, responsible for automatic debits, decided to discontinue the service forcing us to switch to another provider. While this change didn’t affect our operations, we had to dedicate engineering resources to complete the migration successfully. On the positive side, the new provider offers a better and cheaper product.
  • The monthly credit reporting to Experian was delayed due to issues on their end with the file structure and user permissions. The initial report, originally scheduled for end-of-September, was not successfully published until November. Since then, we’ve been able to publish on time every month.

09-07-2024 Credit Hub Latam


We met with them today morning, they will send a couple of comments on the TS to our review. They are aware this is the approved version form our IC but they still have some comments they want to check if we are flexible. In advance they are related to:

  1. Could we define the corporate guarantee to sunset on the bad boy not per our call but defining more objective rules based on covenants or similar?They want to sunset not strictly on our side but if they comply with some metrics/covenants in an specific window of time after 12 months.
  2. They see a risk on the 90 day call option, but they want to know if we could be include some clause to show this is not because a strategy to call the money eventually. I explained to them why we have it but they still see a risk.
  3. The main argument on the previous 2 points and in general terms is because they will expand to Mexico and they are aware that we can’t finance them in Mexico because of Baubap, but they see a risk to find another capital provider if we keep those clauses on the guarantee and the 90 day call option among other comments coming tomorrow in an email.

In general terms, the comments from them are not deal breakers. They will run an extraordinary board meeting in the coming 1 or 2 weeks to get approval to sign the TS, so they expect to sign it off later in July.

7/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

A email was sent today telling them that we will not continue with the process due to lack of engagement.


29/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

An email was sent to a55 asking them if they want to continue with the process. No answers so far.


22/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

AJ is still doing the negotiation


16/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

AJ is still doing the negotiation


2/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

AJ is handling the negotiation.


26/10/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

They are looking for a leverage provider for Senior tranch. They communicated this to AJ. The idea is for them to have senior tranch with a local fund and Mezz tranch with us. AJ sent them a standardized contract to handle this kind of deal. We are waiting for their reply on the contract.


23/10/2023 by LatAM Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

They said \"we were offered this week a potential senior financing compatible with your standard & latest terms,\". Thus, they are waiting for that to work in order to come back to us for the mezz tranch. They said they will come back to us Monday

23/10/2023 with a new model.


18/10/2023 by LatAM Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

We have to reach them several times and they not even reply. It has been almost two weeks of radio silence. AJ gave them a deadline 20/10/2023 to give a reply.


12/10/2023 by LatAM Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Since last week, Felipe has not been answering emails, whatsapp texts or calls. Andres tried to contact Andre today.


5/10/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Andres talked to Andre since Felipe was not answering. Due to this, he got results and obtain answers from them. Felipe had a minor surgery, which explains why he did not not reply. Felipe finally answered and said that he will provide the information to continue with the process this week and he insisted in saying that they are very interested in continuing working with us.  


28/9/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

They offered to provide data regarding the delinquencies and default rates for each franchisee instead of franchisor buckets. We were supposed to receive this information last Friday and we haven't. Felipe texted Andres and let him know that a55 data science department was a late with delivering this information. After this, we have contacted Felipe via whatsapp and email. No respond so far.


21/9/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)AJ,

Andrés and José had a meeting with a55 executives. They offered to provide data regarding the delinquencies and default rates for each fanchisee instead of franchisor buckets. This will provide a more real sense of delinquencies, defaults and concentration. After this information is provided we will talk again about raising interest rates, which they are willing to do. According to Felipe, a55 is still very interested in pursuing with the facility and also according to him we should receive two pieces of information today: new delinquencies and defaults and market research on rates.


14/9/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

We are meeting next tuesday to finish the negotiation of the term sheet.


7/9/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

After several attempts to contact Felipe we received no answers. Thus we contacted Hugo and we had a meeting with him. He said that the board is meeting next week to discuss SixPoint proposal. In the mean time Hugo is figuring out internally if they have a market for a 4.5% simple interest without reducing the quality of the assets.


30/8/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Still waiting for the client for next steps to follow. We discussed the interest rate with them. Andres explained the simple and compound interest rate to client.


24/8/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

13-Feb-2024 by LatAm Hub (JJL, DR, JC)

Moving Klu to Pass due to (AJ comments on Slack):

Their book is heavily concentrated.

Alberto did not present well during our first call.

Not willing to have to deal with Enrique being the “adult” in the room on this deal. Because we will lose him after the deal closes and then we are left with Alberto

Not at all happy about the inter-linking with crypto

Not at all happy about the fact that they’ve not raised any institutional equity

Not happy that Alberto’s father and therefore the family was associated with an alleged fraud

Not happy with the fact that Alberto insists that they process payments they Klu.


06-Feb-2024 by LatAm Hub (JJL, DR, JC)

We are waiting a reply from the lawyers (Alvaro from DLA) and there is a high probability to pass on this deal because of the AML and Reputational risk.


1-Feb-2024 by LatAm Hub (DR, JJL, JC)

We sent a final proposal to the TS including 90days call option and they will reply shortly. We are wating for that reply to see if it is a deal breaker or not.


1/11/2024 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Will be presented to the IC / Variant this week. The pre-flight should be completed by tomorrow. Regarding the TS, we discussed informally some changes to it.


2/1/2024 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Will review preflight internally by 3rd Jan.

Pending information: November financials, Capital K info and Final customer Names.


21/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Klu shared their lawyer contact. AJ sent an email to schedule meeting this week.

Jose talked with Pablo (Albo), CXC and Linq to ask reference.

There is still pending financial statements. We got updated loan tape.


14/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

We had a meeting with them. They agreed to send us the missing information and the lawyer contact. We have not received it yet. In theory, there are no deal breakers regarding the TS signing.


7/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Alberto said that he will have his lawyesr look at the TS and have it back to us. Additionally they sent the TS Markup to review it.

We have almost done the pre-flight. Now it is under AJ revision. We have two main concerns in the last analysis: Concentration limits and stacking, both of them were asked to the client to have a more clear view of those insights.

They want to change the borrower from Klu to Capital K (SOFOM).


29/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

There are no objections to transferring all collection rights and the receivable document to the SPV. KLU will not be collecting anything.

For operational efficiency, they wish to participate in managing the payment channels, noting that MONEX is a competitor.

It has been agreed that our legal team and theirs will discuss and address this particular issue. In addition, it is expected that Klu will become a payment processor (PP) in 2Q 2024 (Note: it will be a PP for its own and client transactions ONLY, not offer it as a third party service). It would be expected that this is acceptable for SixPoint but in the meantime would seek an interim solution while this becomes effective.


We are preparing the pre-flight and they want to sign the TS. They want to send to us ASAP. We will ask AJ about this proposal.


22/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

KLU is analysing the the TS clause that says that all operations must be done via the SPV and that the accounts must be owned by the SPV. We sent them a chart that clarifies this procedure.


16/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

They are reviewing the TS and they will come back to us. They want to put a cap in the profit sharing (AJ said no) and want KLU to be the guarantor not the parent company. AJ said is every company in the structure is a guarantor. This is for the first 12 months. Regarding warrants, AJ said that it will come from the company that raised equity from the VC.


9/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JC)

We sent out the informal proposal and they accepted it. We will send them the TS and we are starting to prepare the preflight memo.



2/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

Pre-screening is almost done. We are just waiting for one date point. We will send first draft of prescreening today.


26/10/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

23/10/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

They sent their operations manual. We will deliver a flow chart model by 23/10/2023. We are waiting to have a meeting with them.


18/10/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

We have received new information and we will have the pre-screening next week.


12/10/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

We had a meeting with them and now they are clear on the information we need. They will send us the information this week at the latest.


5/10/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)

NDA signed and we will get the requested information soon according to them. Their business model seems aligned with our mandate. However, their product is quite profitable, no delinquencies or defaults according to their short data history. It is quite short term (3 days-15 days).


28/9/2023 By LatamHub (JC, AV, JL)

They are one week late with the offer to deliver the information. Today we sent them an email.


20/9/2023 By LatamHub (JC, AV, JL)

The request information was delivered the 5th of this month. They said they will get back to us with that information by the 22nd of this month.

Jose met with Eduardo the CFO and Mercedes the CEO/Founder to talk about the TS:

  1. Main topics they will send comments:
  2. Warrants: The last post-money valuation was $13m then with our proposal the warrants were worth 7% of the company. I offered to do it in the future round they plan to raise in the next 6 months or even a third-party valuation.
  3. Profit Share: They said it seems too high but I explained to them why we have the 15% and our IRR compared with their IRR
  4. Prepayment: They said they could raise debt from the impact funds at a cheaper cost, so they want to have the possibility to replace the senior and keep the mezzanine. I explained to them that it was ok and included in the TS.
  5. Addem is an angel investor and Addem also wants to participate with an off-balance facility circa $2m simultaneously with us. I told them we have no problem with it and they are aware of our relationship with Addem and Pedro Cetina.
  6. They want to meet with you AJ next week, could you give me a couple of alternatives to schedule the meeting?

4-Mar-2024 by LatAm Hub (JJL, DR, JC) We met with Felipe+Felipe and they made the decision to continue with the TS they received from a Family office (Katz FO) in Panama for $4m and a maximum advance rate of 85%, fixed interest rate of 18% in USD. (3 tranches 75%, 80% and 85%) The main issue with our proposal is the low advance rate, but they are sure they want to reengage in june/july when they have more track record and when they decrease the average tenor in their loan book.


12-Feb-2024 by LatAm Hub (JJL, DR, JC) We had a meeting with Welli and they showed interest in the term sheets sent last week. They were worried about a 9% equity share warrant, but we told them this is negotiable. They also told us that they estimated a 32% interest rate of the facility but we told them that it wasn’t the case. and we updated. They told us that they were going to calculate the mix of product and come back to us.


06-Feb-2024 by LatAm Hub (JJL, DR, JC) We will send the proposal and the TS today


1-Feb-2024 by LatAm Hub (DR, JJL, JC) AJ met in person with the founders, then we made an update to the preflight and we are building a power point presentation in order to send the TS and the presentation today.


10/1/2024 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) Emailed Felipe if they feel confortable with deductible commission to patient (5-10%). They do not consider it appropriate. But they think FGA could raise up to ~10% (And potentially more as the usury rate evolves). Additionally, they can consider collecting an advance payment of part of the security deposit (rather than the same monthly amount as they currently do). 2/1/2024 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) Contact Felipe if they feel confortable with upfront fee. Prepare Term Sheet.


21/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) The latest version of Pricer, which allows us to set advanced rates on \"remaining maturity\" is already done. We are using Strict DPD calculations from Cascade. Today will send preflight memo to AJ. We did some follow up questions to Welli, regarding loan tape.


14/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) The pricer modification is almost done. The Cascade strict DPD delinquency ratio template is also almost done. We expect to have the pre-flight by next week.


7/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) We met with them and the only objection of the 3 conditions is the “Libranzas” condition. They mentioned they want to focus on the current product but in the future they will consider it as a new product. We will negotiate wiht them a TS before building the pre-flight. They are working on the auto-deduct feature using automatic debit from bank accounts and they already have in place the “Fondo de Garantias” feature.


1/12/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) We sent Welli 3 conditions to continue with the process. We are waiting for a reply.


29/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) yesterday we met with Welli to present them our new proposal: • Advance rate per product. • 24 months maximum loan term. • The weight on the portfolio for the 24-month product, after one year, should be 50%.Meeting minute: • Welli would like to initiate the due diligence process with the aim of progressing until we have sufficient data for SixPoint to feel comfortable financing a portfolio with longer terms. • Dixit from felipe: As part of this process, we would set some milestones that you would like to see, and we could start working on a conditional term sheet. • Welli is ok with advance rate per product. • Welli av loan term is 24 months. They will continue pushing towards shorter terms, but they see our proposal is still far from their possibility (our average proposal is 16 months). Welli’s target customer requires a longer term due to the income-to-installment ratio (for reference, see below email from Felipe explaining how they calculate quotas/term). • Welli is in talks with providers to implement automatic debit. The possible degree of acceptance by the end user is still unknown. • They are aware of Deceval system but find it challenging to implement because it requires agreements with each employer. Customers do not come through employers but rather through referrals from clinics/doctors. We are waiting for AJ to gives us the green light to start the preflight.


22/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) The pricer has been modified to have a variable AR for products.


16/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) Pre TS proposal has been sent today


9/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC)We started to build the prescreening. The first draft will be ready early next week.


2/11/2023 by LatAm Hub (AV, JJL, JC) AJ had the intro Call, and the LatAm team will meet with them in the next days.

Tuily pasa a Pass. Debajo mail enviado al cliente explicando los motivos.



From: Juan Jose Lanzarotti

Sent: Friday, April 26, 2024 3:49 PM

To: marcela@tuily.com; Jonathan Tarud <jonathan@tuily.com>

Cc: Marcos Impala <marcos@sixpoint.io>; Diego Ramirez <diego.ramirez@sixpoint.io>; Juan Pablo Donoso <donoso@optiks.com.co>; Mateo Marulanda <mateo@optiks.com.co>; Jose Colorado <jose@sixpoint.io>

Subject: RE: NDA y solicitud de información


Marcela / Jonathan, buenas tardes,

 

Hemos analizado los unit economics de Tuily y por el momento tomamos la decisión de no continuar con el proceso. Comparto los motivos de la decisión:

 

Pricing:

  • Intercharge fee es bajo para el plazo que operan. (8 meses promedio según información compartida previamente)
  • No vemos otras fuentes de revenue que compensen pricing.

 

Default:

  • Actualmente 6% de default y en sus proyecciones aspiran a 5%. Números elevador en comparación con lo que vemos en plataformas similares en Colombia y México, donde con plazos de 1 mes y créditos revolving, el default se encuentra en torno al 1% (y duplican pricing de Tuily).
  • Con default a estos niveles, hace que el fondo de garantías quede bajo en proporción con el default.
  • Este nivel de default indica que deben continuar trabajando sobre la política de Underwriting y mejorando la metodología de scoring.

 

Originación:

  • Nuestro facility comienza en USD 10m. Por las originaciones a la fecha y sus proyecciones, en conjunto con los puntos mencionados anteriormente, lo vemos grande para la etapa actual de la compañia.

 

 

Les deseamos éxitos en los próximos pasos.

 

Con mucho gusto podemos volver a contactarnos en un futuro, con un track record suficiente que refleje los puntos mencionados en el loan book.

 

 

Saludos,

 

Juan Lanzarotti

Credit team LATAM

Hola Jose,


Como te comentamos estamos trabajando fuertemente para salir live con el cobro de FGA en las próximas dos semanas de acuerdo al estimado del equipo técnico.


En cuanto a tus preguntas, te respondo:

1.     Unit economics: adjunto encuentras un archivo detallado de cómo vemos que están los unit economics del producto y cómo mejorarían una vez podamos retomar crecimiento. En este momento tenemos un gross yield del 6.5%, y un gross profit del 2.7 pps mensuales de la cartera colocada

2.     Interest rate: estamos cobrando usura menos 2 pps

3.     Fees: interchange fee del 1.7%

5.     Defaults: en este momento tenemos niveles de mora de 6% de originación, esperamos que los defaults queden en ese sentido en niveles del 2.5%

Déjenos saber un par de alternativas de horario en el que les podamos recorrer el archivo de unit economics si es que les surgen inquietudes y quedamos atentos a los próximos pasos.


Gracias,


Marcela Azcárate
